messages.author: a0bba3d134bd351f
messages.subject: Labeling in make.lincombs
parts:
Hey Guys,

I'm trying to get the posterior correlation matrix of all random effects (long story), and I seem to be hitting a labeling issue in make.lincombs.  Here's a simple example of what I'm doing

library(INLA)
set.seed(1)

p <- 5
rho <- .9
sig <- sqrt(1 - .9^2)
Y <- rnorm(1,0,sig)
for(i in 2:p)Y[i] <- rho * Y[i - 1] + rnorm(1,0,sd=sig)
D <- as.data.frame(cbind(1:p,Y))
names(D) <- c("ID","Y")

formula <- Y ~ f(ID,model = "ar1") - 1

lc.many <- inla.make.lincombs(ID = diag(p))  ##Potentially incorrect?

a <- inla(formula,"gaussian",data = D,
          lincomb = lc.many,
          control.predictor = list(compute = TRUE),
          control.inla = list(lincomb.derived.correlation.matrix = TRUE)
          )

b <- a$misc$lincomb.derived.correlation.matrix
print(round(b,3))

This returns

       lc1    lc2    lc3    lc4    lc5
lc1  1.000 -0.003  0.399  0.000  0.324
lc2 -0.003  1.000 -0.003  0.399  0.000
lc3  0.399 -0.003  1.000 -0.003  0.399
lc4  0.000  0.399 -0.003  1.000 -0.003
lc5  0.324  0.000  0.399 -0.003  1.000

The numbers are sort of fine, but it seems like the spacing is off.  In particular, it would seem like the value in (1,3) should be in (1,2) and (1,5) should be in (1,3).  Am I doing something wrong when I set up the lin.comb object?

Thanks!

Alex

messages.author: a0bba3d134bd351f
messages.subject: Re: Labeling in make.lincombs
parts:
Hi All,

This turned out to be a misunderstanding on my part.  The matrix returned would not have had the AR1 structure because the Y was observed.  Thus, the correlation matrix that was returned is more like the residual correlation matrix after the AR1 model.

Sorry about that guys, and thanks for the clarification.

Alex

messages.subject: Re: Labeling in make.lincombs
parts:
Hi Everyone,

Many thanks to Håvard and Finn for helpful comments.  Just for everyone's info, what's below does what I was looking for.

rm(list = ls())
library(INLA)
set.seed(1)


n.1 <- 1e3
n.2 <- 5

Y <- rnorm(1,0,1) ## Finn pointed out this was wrong before
for(i in 2:n.1)Y[i] <- rho * Y[i - 1] + rnorm(1,0,sd=sig)
Y[(n.1 + 1):(n.1 + n.2)] <- NA
D <- data.frame(cbind(1:(n.1 + n.2),Y))

A <- diag(n.1 + n.2)
A <- A[,(n.1 + 1):(n.1 + n.2)]
lc.many <- inla.make.lincombs(ID = t(A))

a <- inla(formula,"gaussian",data = D,
          lincomb = lc.many,
          control.predictor = list(compute = TRUE),
          control.inla = list(lincomb.derived.correlation.matrix = TRUE)
          )

b <- a$misc$lincomb.derived.correlation.matrix

print(round(b,3))

This returns

      lc1   lc2   lc3   lc4   lc5
